I N T R O D U C T I ON 
  
I,  the Chairman of the Department-related Parl iamentary Standing Committee on Industry,  having  
been authorised  by the Committe e, hereby present this One Hundr ed –Thirty fourth Report on the 
Action Taken by the Government on the recommenda tions contained in  the  Committee ' s  119 th  
Report  on Demands for Grants (2003-2004) pertaining to Department of Public Enterprises (Ministry of
Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises). 
  
2.         The Committee   examined and  c onsidered  the Action Take n Notes on recommendations
contained  in  Committee’s the   119 th  Report  on Demands for Gran ts (2003-2004) pertaining to 
Department of Public Enterprises (Ministry of Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises).  
  
3.        This Action Taken Report has been prepar ed on the basis of the acti on taken note furnished by
the Department of Public Enterp rises (Ministry of Heavy Industrie s and Public Enterprises) on the
recommendations contained in the Committee’s 119 th Report.  The Committee adopted the analytical 
and descriptive approach to exam ine the action taken notes and afte r assessing the action taken note as 
furnished by the Department of Public Enterprises (Ministry of Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises)
and judging the same in the true spirit of the recommendations,  the Committee has prepared the present
Action Taken Report. Action taken notes have been an alyzed and suitably categorized in four chapters
in the Action Taken Report and the Observations/C onclusions and Recommendations of the Committee
have been placed in Chapter – V. 
  
4.         The Committee at its meeting held on 18th December, 2003 considered and adopted the Report.

CHAPTER - I 
  
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS ACCEPTED BY THE GOVERNMENT 
  
  
1.1       INCREASE IN THE PLAN ALLOCATION of CRR SCHEME 
  
RECOMMENDATION 
  
The Committee finds that there has been consta nt increase in the pl an allocation of CRR Sc h
over the earlier years.  As agains t Rs. 6.75 crores allocated in RE 2001-02, an allocation of Rs. 8.50 c r
was made in BE 2002-03 for CRR which was ta ken up by DPE since 1 st April 2001.  Earlier it was dea l
the Department of Industrial Policy & Promotion.  In BE 2003-04, the amount has been increased to Rs. 9
crores.  This is the third year since the scheme commenced.  The Committee recommends that in view of
increasing trends in the plan allocation for CRR scheme and time factor, a suitable mechanism for appr a
of the scheme should be evolved by DPE so as to ev aluate the results in this  regard and assess the de s
impact of the scheme.  
                                                                                                            (Para No. 3.4 )               
ACTION TAKEN 
  
  
1.1.1   Two years of CRR scheme have been complete d. With the objective to have an appraisal o f
Scheme by a neutral and autonomous organisation, process has been in itiated in regard to selectio n
Institution/organization to undertake efficacy study of the selected noda l agencies to ev aluate the impa c
the scheme and to bring about further improvements.  
RECOMMENDATION 
  
1.2    Allocation of Funds for CRR Scheme in the North East region 
  
The Committee observes that North Eastern Ar ea and Sikkim comprising of seven states 
Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Naga land, Assam, Tripura, Manipur an d Mizoram, is an economically 
industrially backward area. The al location of Rs. 1.00 crores for th e area for CRR scheme is not en o
considering the vast area to be covered under the sc heme.  If the area has to be developed, entrepreneur
has to be given a fillip.  The Co mmittee, therefore, reco mmends that the plan allocation for North Ea s
area should be further increased so as to open more training centers in these ar eas to impart training t o
persons and have a wider coverage of the scheme.                         
                                                                        (Para No. 3.6)
ACTION TAKEN 
1.2.1   In order to implement the CRR programme in the North East Region, for the first time, DPE sele
a Nodal Agency viz., Indian Instit ute of Entrepreneurship, Guwahati . As per the extant norms 10% o f
total sanctioned fund has been earm arked for the N.E. Region. Accord ingly, out of total fund allocate d

CRR scheme for the year 2002- 2003 and 2003-2004, Rs. 1 crore each is  earmarked for the region. W i
view to further widen the coverage in the NE Region, another centre at Guwahati was started by NPC du
2002-03. However, North Eastern Region has specific problems mainly because of very few number of u
of CPSEs in the region and less number of available VRS optees.  Bo th operating agencies in NE Re g
have been directed to explore possibilities to identify more numbers of VR Optees for CRR Scheme. 
  
RECOMMENDATION 
  
1.3  Role of DPE in evaluation  of  MOU System 
  
The Committee recommends that DPE should reor ient and reorganise its  activities as far as
signing of MOU is concerned.  The si gning of MOUs should not be a me re formal exercise.  DPE needs
to reassess and revaluate its role in so far as  MOU is concerned. The Co mmittee further, recommends
that the signing of MOU sh ould continue to be with DPE with a view to have uniform method o f
evaluation of CPSEs. 
                                                                                                                        (Para No. 7.6)
ACTION TAKEN 
1.3.1   The MOU system is bei ng implemented since 1987-88 and during this period a number o f 
changes has taken place which aff ected the over all economic and bus iness environment both in the
domestic and international market. Keeping in view the changing e nvironment, DPE has made certain
efforts to make the MOU system a dynamic mech anism to evaluate the performance of the
managements of the PSEs. As a pa rt of these efforts emphasis was laid on dynamic para meters such as
marketing, modernisation, technol ogical upgradation, quality control,  customers satisfaction and R&D
etc.  to ensure that PSEs not onl y strengthen their operations over a long period of time but also face the
challenges of market economy.  The PSEs have alre ady been instructed to adopt international
benchmarks of efficiency and quality in their respect ive areas of operations so  that their comparative
evaluation is not only confined to th eir past performance but also reflects their standing as compared to
the other players in the market. The working of MOU System, the choice of performance criteria and the
allocation of weight to di fferent performance parameters is bei ng reviewed and suitable changes would
be incorporated from next year. 
  
RECOMMENDATION 
  
1.4   Critical factors in the MOU parameters

The Committee recommends that Department of Public Enterpri ses should analyse the factors
critical in the MOU parameters while grading their performance a nd suggest to the Administrative
Ministries in appropriate manner how their pe rformance can be improved, otherwise MOU signing
merely becomes a ritual which has nothing to offer for improvement of PSEs 
                                                                                                                        (Para No. 7.7)
ACTION TAKEN 
1.4.1   During the MOU negotiation meetings a great deal  of discussion takes place on the sectoral
issues, past performa nce of the PSE and emerging threats and opportunities in  the particular area in
which a PSE is operating.  During the meetings va rious valuable suggestions are given to the
Administrative Ministry and PSEs and the progress on these suggest ions is reviewed in the subsequent
meetings.  The inputs generated dur ing these MOU negotiation meetings  are widely appreciated by the
PSEs as well as by the Administrative Ministries.  
  
RECOMMENDATION 
  
1.5   Investment decisions on social cost benefit analysis 
  
The Committee observes that the i nvestment decisions to create public sector units were based
on social cost benefit analysis.  Moreover, most of the public sector  enterprises were not expected to
maximise profits.  However, the social cause no l onger being in vogue, and mark et forces replacing the
old economy with the ushering in of liberalisation, the performance of PSEs has to be evaluated on thei r
economic performance.  The public sector enterprises performance, therefore, should be evaluated based
on their financial profit. 
                                                                                                            (Para No. 7.13)
ACTION TAKEN 
1.5.1  The spirit behind this reco mmendation of the Committee is a ppreciated. With the changes in
economic environment, efforts have been made to make the MOU sy stem a dynamic instrument to meet
the emerging requirements. The initiatives taken thr ough the MOU system have th e focus to prepare the
PSEs to face the emerging compet itive scenario by introducing the dynamic parameters. However, the
parameters relating to profitabil ity and financial position of th e Company, continues to get the
significant weightage.

RECOMMENDATION 
  
1.6    MOU system as an instrument of  performance improvement. 
The Committee appreciates the effort s of DPE to make the MOU system  more effective.  Still much
more has to be done in this direct ion.  It is more important that dynamic parameters like productivity,
customer satisfaction, HRD, quali ty improvement and R&D are take n into account.  Department o f
Public Enterprises should constantly endeavour to make the MOU system as an instrument o f
improvement. 
                                                                                                                    (Para No. 7.16) 
ACTION TAKEN 
1.6.1 Dynamic performance parameters recommended by the Co mmittee like Productivity, Custome r
satisfaction, HRD, Marketing, R&D, Project Implementation, etc. have been in cluded in the guidelines
issued by DPE to MOU signing and Administrative Ministries/Depar tments for drafting their MOU
documents and they have been advised to include th ese parameters, which are crucial for their long term
health, in the respective MOUs. During the MOU ne gotiation meetings, detailed discussion regarding
the choice of suitable performance parameters and the weights assigned to them takes place. 
  
1.6.2 DPE will continue its efforts to further improve the MOU system for the ensuing year, based upon
past experience and advice of experts.

Enterprises compile the quarterly information rega rding implementation of the policy by the Central

apprised accordingly.  Information for the 1 st and 2 nd quarters of 2002-03 were  furnished vide DPE’s

RECOMMENDATION 
  
1.8      Treating VRS funds as grants 
  
The Committee recommends that Govt. should revert  to the old system of  treating VRS funds as
grants.  It would be a much needed relief as lo ss making and marginally profit making Companies are in
urgent need of shedding their oversized manpower.   
                                                                                                            (Para No. 10.1)
ACTION TAKEN 
1.8.1   Before introduction of revised VRS polic y in May, 2000 VRS was funded through National
Renewal Fund (NRF) which has ceased to exist in  May, 2000. Under the revised VR scheme there is
provision for budgetary support to the sick enterprises and under certain circumstances to the marginally
profit or loss making enterprises also for implementing VRS.

RECOMMENDATION
 
  
2.1  Financial performance as the main criteria for rating their achievement 
  
MOU should have relation to financ ial well being of a PSEs.  Fi nancial parameters are must to
evaluate the state of health of a PSE.  However, the Committee observes that PSEs which are even under
performing are graded as good, very good or excelle nt depending upon the level of their achievements
under the MOU target.  Th e Committee, therefore, recommends that financial performance of PSEs
should be the main criteria for rating their achievement. 
                                                                                                            (Para No. 7.14)
ACTION TAKEN 
2.1.1  In respect of the PSEs operating under compet itive conditions the fi nancial parameters are
assigned 60% weight which is quite significant. In fact, the pe rformance of the PSEs under the MOU
system is evaluated on 5 point scale basis and for each grade targets are indicated well in advance.  The
grading of Excellent, Very Good, G ood and so on represents the level of performance on the above said
5-point scale.  In fact, the evaluation mechanis m under the MOU system trie s to strike a balance
between financial and non-financial parameters.  
  
CHAPTER - III 
  
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH THE COMMITTEE
HAS NOT ACCEPTED REPLIES OF THE DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC ENTERPRISES. 
  
RECOMMENDATION 
  
3.1   Training for VRS optee employees 
  
The Committee recommends that training for VRS optee employees should be organized in such
a way as they can create self-employment in the smal l scale sector and avail th e benefit of the schemes 
like PMRY, REGP etc. in the small and tiny se ctor. Counselling, retraini ng and redeployment ( CRR)
scheme has now taken roots.  The Co mmittee feels that there is an urge nt need to increase its spread to
cover at least 40, 000 workers per a nnum in addition to covering a back log of about 1 lakh workers.  In
this context, the Committee recomm ends that steps are urgently requi red for allocation of funds for the
scheme which needs to be at leas t doubled.  Ministry of Heavy Industries should al so ensure that PSEs

shall clear all their dues before relieving them from the organisati on so that they can plan thei r
future course of action in earni ng livelihood in the new environment.  Ministry of Finance should issue
direction that banks honour their fi nancial requirements in the aftermath of VRS/ VSS to avail of the
small sector employment schemes.  The workers separated on VRS should be entitled to borrowing from
commercial banks under the priority sector lending dispensation.   
                                                                                                (Para No. 3.11)
ACTION TAKEN 
3.1.1   Keeping in view the growing number of VR optees year after year, a llocation of fund for CR R
scheme needs to be enhanced substantially. This De partment has been making efforts in this direction.
There is standing instruction to all the CPSUs that before relieving the employees opting for VR, all the
dues should be paid. For prope r implementation of the CRR Scheme, Coordination Committees
comprising of head of the units of  CPSUs, nodal agencies, lead bank ha ve been formed at local level
which also take care of borrowing from commercial banks to carry out self-employment activities.  
Ministry of Finance has been request ed to issue suitable instructions to the commercial Banks in regard
to linking credit with CRR Scheme. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION 
  
3.1.2   The Committee keeping in view the growing num ber of VR optees year after year, (in addition to
covering a backlog of about 1 lakh workers)is of th e considered view that  allocation of fund for CR R
scheme needs to be enhanced substantially.  Th e Committee recommends th at training for VRS optee
employees should be organized in su ch a way as they can create se lf-employment in the small scale 
sector and avail the benefi t of the schemes like PMRY, REGP etc.  in the small and tiny sector.  The
Committee further desires that th e Ministry of Finance should issu e direction that banks honour thei r
financial requirements in the afterm ath of VRS/VSS to avail of the small sector employment schemes. 
The workers separated on VRS should be entitled to borrowing from commercial banks under the
priority sector lending dispensation.  Pl aying its pro-active ro le the Department of Public Enterprises is 
required to forward the matter to the Ministry of Finance in a result oriented manner.

RECOMMENDATION 
  
3.4   Revival and rejuvenation of sick PSEs 
  
The Committee observes that at pr esent there are 240 Central Public  Sector Enterprises.  If the
percentage figure of MOU signed PSEs is taken, it is less than 50% now .  Sick PSEs are debarred from

signing MOU.  The Committee would have appreciated if DPE would provide necessary
logistical support like technical assistance to sick PSEs to revive and rejuvenate them. 
                                                                                                                        (Para No. 7.8)
ACTION TAKEN 
3.4.1  Every year about 100 PSEs sign the MOU with their respective Administrative
Ministries/Departments. Many of th ese PSEs are holding Companies and if  their subsidiaries are taken
into account, the number of the PSEs covered under the MOU system, works out  to about 150. Many
loss making PSEs also sign MOUs, however, the sick PSEs referred to BIFR, small and insignificant
PSEs and the PSEs, which are under construction, are not covered under the MOU system.  
3.4.2   Consequent upon the amendment of the Sick  Industrial Companies Act (SICA), 1985, the sic k
industrial public sector enterprises are referred to the Board for Industrial & Financial Reconstruction
(BIFR). The BIFR appoin t operating agency in eac h case for preparing re vival package for sic k
industrial companies. On the basis of the recomme ndations of the operating agency, which are finalised
in consultation with various concerned parties including promoters, the revival package is sanctioned by
the BIFR, as per the provisions of SICA a nd implemented by the concerned administrative
Ministry/Department. Thus, BI FR is a nodal agency which provides necessary support through
operating agency and other financial institutions for the revival of sick PSEs under the provisions of law.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION  
  
3.4.3   The Committee is of the c onsidered view that since Sick PSEs are debarred from signing MOU,
DPE should come forward to  provide necessary logistical support like technical assistance to sick PSEs 
for their  revival  and rejuvenati on.  The Committee is of the view th at generally the cycles of coming
out of sick PSEs  from the purview  of BIFR takes a  long spell of time.  So, in order to avoid the
procrastination  in the revival of si ck PSEs the Department of Public Enterprises must play the role o f
facilitator.

for no monetary gain.  Committee has the apprehension that he may play down on their accountability to
the Board of PSE of which they are members.  DPE should look into this aspect.

3.5.3  The Committee is of the view that the professionalisation of Board of Directors  is the sine-qu-non

segments of society i.e. public men, technocrats., mana gement experts posses a question mark on the
efficiency and effectiveness in the decision making of corporate go vernance. The Board of Directors
should be a body of expert s having in depth understanding of the global corporate rules and practices of
managerial  skill in order to obtain the global standard  of corporate governance.  Therefore, the
Committee’s  apprehension of  the nomination of part time Directors on the Board of Directors does not
come to the expectations of working of corporate world.  That is why the Committee recommends that
the Department of Public Enterprises in consulta tion with the Department of Company Affairs should
chalk out the alternative arrangement of  non-official part-time director s for generating better corporate 
governance in the PSEs.

financial requirements in the afterm ath of VRS/VSS to avail of the small sector employment schemes.
